normalized.governing_thought: Yes: raise prices in 2027, but by segment: 10% at mid-market and 7–10% at enterprise renewals, with SMB held until a test proves it
executive_summary: Yes: raise prices in 2027, but by segment: 10% at mid-market and 7–10% at enterprise renewals, with SMB held until a test proves it

1 Churn is rising because of the 2025 SMB promotion, not because customers reject today's prices – SMB monthly logo churn rose from 2.0% to 3.1%; enterprise held at 0.2% – Non-promotion SMB churn is 2.1% a month, against 2.0% a year earlier – Only 18% of non-promotion churners cite price, against 52% in the cohort (p. 4–6)

2 Mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise; SMB, under pressure from Inkwell, cannot yet – A 10% list-price test left mid-market conversion statistically unchanged – Where Inkwell competes, our SMB win rate fell from 51% to 38% (p. 8–10)

3 The CFO's flat 12% yields about $7.6M, not $10.3M; a segmented rise adds about $4.3M – Renewal timing and the 7% enterprise cap cut $10.3M to about $7.6M – With today's retention, that leaves only $0.6M of new ARR to find for 15% growth – Each rise pays unless it loses nearly twice the customers 2023's did (p. 12–14)

4 Hold SMB prices until a Q1 2027 test, and activate the promotion cohort instead – A fixed promotion cohort would cut SMB churn by a third, from 3.1% to 2.1% – An 8% test on non-promotion SMB could add up to $1.3M once it passes (p. 16, 17)

slides.title: Why churn is rising
Rising churn is concentrated in SMB, while mid-market and enterprise still grow revenue from existing customers

claims.claim: SMB is where churn rose: up by more than half in a year, and the only segment keeping less than 100% of its revenue
evidence: SMB: 5,900 customers; $21M ARR; monthly logo churn 2% H1 2025, 3.1% H1 2026; NRR 94%

claims.claim: Mid-market: churn up slightly; revenue from existing customers still grows
evidence: Mid-market: 1,350 customers; $41M ARR; churn 0.6% → 0.8%; NRR 112%

claims.claim: Enterprise: churn flat; the strongest expansion
evidence: Enterprise: 150 customers; $24M ARR; churn 0.2% → 0.2%; NRR 118%

claims.claim: The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" does not define its measure and cannot be rebuilt from these figures (backup)

slides.title: The 2025 promotion cohort drives the SMB rise, churning at more than twice the rate of other SMB customers

claims.claim: One cohort moved, not the whole SMB base
evidence: SMB monthly logo churn H1 2026: Promotion cohort (est.) 4.9%; All SMB 3.1%; Non-promotion SMB 2.1%; Non-promotion SMB H1 2025 2.0%
2.3x promotion-cohort churn as a multiple of other SMB customers' churn, H1 2026 (estimate)

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: 2,100 customers who joined at 50% off in February–August 2025; most leavers went within two months of the discount ending
evidence: Estimate: SMB lost a month 183 (3.1% × 5,900) − non-promotion lost 80 (2.1% × 3,800) ÷ 2,100 promotion-cohort customers = 4.9% cohort monthly churn

claims.claim: Non-promotion SMB: essentially flat against the H1 2025 line, so the core SMB base has not turned against Palisade
All SMB: the blend rises because the cohort is now 36% of SMB customers

slides.title: Most promotion customers never set up the product and quit when full price arrived; other churners cite price as before

claims.claim: Fewer than half of promotion customers ever set up the product
evidence: Activated in month one: Promotion cohort 41%; Other cohorts 72%
SMB customers below that [activation threshold] churn at about three times the rate of the rest

claims.claim: Price complaints rose only among promotion-cohort churners
evidence: Churners citing price: All SMB H1 2025 19%; All SMB H1 2026 34%; Promotion cohort H1 2026 52%; Non-promotion H1 2026 18%

claims.claim: Both views hold for this cohort: it needs onboarding, and it is the one group that reacts to price

slides.title: Where Palisade has pricing power
Three signs say mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise, led by a price test that left conversion unchanged

claims.claim: A 10% higher list price left mid-market conversion unchanged
evidence: 23.1% conversion of mid-market sign-ups offered a 10% higher list price, 2024
Against 23.6% for the control group; the gap is not statistically significant
Three-month test on new mid-market sign-ups only

claims.claim: Enterprise retains 118%: both segments grow from existing customers
evidence: 112% mid-market net revenue retention, trailing 12 months
Monthly logo churn of 0.8% in mid-market and 0.2% in enterprise, H1 2026
Customers name integrations and the audit trail as their main reasons to stay (advisory board, 2026)

claims.claim: The low-price rival competes in SMB, not with larger buyers
evidence: 200 seats: Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals above this size
Inkwell's plans list at $9 (Starter) and $24 (Pro) per user per month
Larger buyers weigh the integrations and audit trail they say keep them

claims.claim: The tested 10%, not an untested 12%, is the level to use in 2027

−13 pp
Inkwell Starter launched in October 2025

claims.claim: A 12% rise would price the SMB plan at almost twice Inkwell Starter
evidence: List price per user per month: Inkwell Starter $9; Palisade SMB today $15; Palisade SMB after 12% $16.8
Palisade's Business plan lists at $29 against Inkwell Pro at $24

claims.claim: In SMB the open question is whether customers will pay a growing premium over Inkwell, and nobody has measured it yet

slides.title: SMB absorbed the 2023 rise with a six-month churn spike, but that precedent predates Inkwell

claims.claim: A temporary spike, measured before a cheap rival existed
evidence: SMB monthly logo churn: Before the 2023 rise 1.8%; First six months after 2.3%; After it settled 1.9%
2023 rise: +8% on SMB plans at renewal

claims.claim: After it settled: churn stayed just above the old level, the lasting cost of the 8% rise
Since then: Inkwell's $9 Starter plan may have made SMB customers more price-sensitive; nobody has measured how much
For 2027: a renewal test on part of non-promotion SMB, not a blanket rise, is how to learn the new response

slides.title: What a rise is worth
Renewal timing and contract caps cut the CFO's $10.3M to about $7.6M before any customer reacts

claims.claim: Renewal timing and contract caps cut the CFO's $10.3M to about $7.6M
evidence: CFO figure: 12% on all ARR 10.3; Mid-market renewing after 2027 −0.738; Enterprise renewing after 2027 −1.728; Enterprise 7% cap −0.288; Reachable at 2027 renewals 7.566 ($M)
CFO figure = 12% × $86.0M of ARR
60% of enterprise ARR renews after 2027
15% of [mid-market] ARR renews after 2027
capped contracts can rise only 7%
$2.5M SMB (12% × $21.0M) + $4.2M mid-market (12% × 85% of $41.0M) + $0.9M enterprise (7% or 12% on renewals) = $7.6M reachable before churn response

claims.claim: What is left leans on the riskiest segment
evidence: 33% of the reachable uplift would come from SMB
Promotion cohort: $0.5M of the gain would come from these 2,100 customers

slides.title: At today's retention, a segmented rise leaves only about $0.6M of new ARR to find for the 2027 growth target

claims.claim: The target is in reach without touching SMB prices
evidence: ARR mid-2026 86; Existing customers at today's NRR +8; Mid-market +10% at renewal +3.485; Enterprise +7–10% at renewal +0.7872; New business needed 0.6278; 2027 target 98.9 ($M)
$98.9M (target: +15% on $86.0M) − $94M (at today's NRR) − $3.5M (mid-market: 10% × $34.9M) − $0.8M (enterprise: 7% or 10%) = $0.6M new ARR still needed
114% overall net revenue retention with the rise, against a floor of 100%

claims.claim: Existing customers: mid-market and enterprise expansion carries the base even though SMB retains only 94%
Price: the two segment moves supply about a third of the growth the target needs
Against the CFO plan: 12% everywhere would add about $3.3M more on paper, three-quarters of it from SMB

slides.title: Even the smallest rise keeps paying unless it drives away nearly twice the customers the 2023 rise did

claims.claim: Churn would have to jump far beyond any past response
evidence: Break-even extra loss: Enterprise, capped +7%: 6.5%; SMB test +8%: 7.4%; Mid-market and other enterprise +10%: 9.1%; 2023 SMB rise extra loss in year one (est.): 3.6%
Smallest break-even ÷ 2023 extra loss: 1.8x (6.5% ÷ 3.6%)
2023 extra loss: 3% (spike: 0.5 pp a month × 6) + 0.6% (months 7–12: 0.1 pp × 6) = 3.6% extra SMB loss, year one

claims.claim: Rule: a rise of p pays while it loses fewer than p ÷ (1 + p) of renewing customers
Mid-market: break-even is about a year of today's churn at 0.8% a month
SMB: the 2023 rise stayed well inside its break-even; the test checks if Inkwell changed that

slides.title: How to protect SMB
Fixing the promotion cohort would cut SMB churn by about a third, not the half Customer Success expects

claims.claim: Fixing the promotion cohort would cut SMB churn by about a third, not the half Customer Success expects
evidence: SMB monthly logo churn: SMB today H1 2026 3.1%; If the cohort churned like other SMB 2.1%; Halved, as Customer Success expects 1.55%
32% cut in SMB churn if the cohort churned like other SMB
Halved: needs non-promotion churn far below its 2.0–2.1%
Customer Success expects an onboarding programme to halve SMB churn within two quarters; the briefing pack gives no evidence for the size of the effect

claims.claim: Activation helps, but it is not a pricing plan
evidence: Lever: 41% of the cohort activated, against 72% of other cohorts

claims.claim: Set 2027 prices on today's churn; count activation gains as upside

slides.title: Sequencing turns the CEO's churn worry into a gate: larger segments move first, SMB only after a first-quarter test

evidence: Leadership team: Approve the segmented plan (Dec 2026); SMB go / no-go
Mid-market and enterprise: +10% at mid-market renewals; +7–10% at enterprise renewals
Non-promotion SMB: 8% test on part of renewals (Q1 2027); Extend only if losses stay inside break-even
Promotion cohort: Activation programme; price held; Review price once activated
Board reporting: One defined churn measure, by segment, every month

claims.claim: Stop rule: pause any rise whose renewal losses approach its break-even, starting with the monthly mid-market read
An 8% rise on all non-promotion SMB renewals would add up to $1.3M of ARR if the test passes

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices in 2027 by segment: +10% at mid-market renewals and +7–10% at enterprise renewals from January 2027, with SMB held until a test proves it; hold SMB prices until a Q1 2027 test (8% renewal test on part of non-promotion SMB) and activate the promotion cohort instead.

alternatives_considered.option: CFO's flat 12% rise on every plan
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: The CFO's flat 12% yields about $7.6M, not $10.3M; renewal timing and contract caps cut it; what is left leans on the riskiest segment (33% from SMB); 12% everywhere would add about $3.3M more on paper, three-quarters of it from SMB; the tested 10%, not an untested 12%, is the level to use.

alternatives_considered.option: Segmented rise: +10% mid-market, +7–10% enterprise, SMB held pending test
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: adds about $4.3M; leaves only about $0.6M of new ARR to find for the 2027 growth target; the target is in reach without touching SMB prices.

Rejected in favour of a renewal test on part of non-promotion SMB: 'a renewal test on part of non-promotion SMB, not a blanket rise, is how to learn the new response'; SMB under pressure from Inkwell cannot yet carry a rise.

alternatives_considered.option: Rely on Customer Success onboarding programme halving SMB churn
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected as a basis for pricing: fixing the cohort would cut SMB churn by about a third, not the half Customer Success expects; no evidence for the size of the effect; set 2027 prices on today's churn and count activation gains as upside.
Not used: measure not defined and cannot be rebuilt from segment data, so the deck uses segment logo churn; replace it with one defined measure, by segment.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the Palisade briefing pack
Promotion-cohort churn is an estimate using mid-2026 customer counts as the average H1 2026 base
Mid-market price test was a three-month test on new sign-ups only; how existing customers react at renewal is still untested
Whether SMB customers will pay a growing premium over Inkwell has not been measured; Inkwell may have made SMB customers more price-sensitive; nobody has measured how much
The briefing pack gives no churn readings for the months in between around the 2023 rise
NRR: trailing 12 months to mid-2026, applied once; SMB's 94% may include promotion discounts ending, which will not repeat
Price steps assume no extra churn and 60% of renewing enterprise ARR capped
Reachable uplift is before churn response; price changes apply only at renewal, and enterprise contracts follow their own terms
Customer Success's expected halving of SMB churn has no evidence for the size of the effect in the briefing pack
Weighted churn averages use mid-2026 customers and ARR for both periods; the briefing pack has no H1 2025 segment weights
The board dashboard churn measure is not defined and cannot be rebuilt
The 2023 extra-loss figure is an estimate
